item.title: Re: Partha Kar: Expanding roles of healthcare staff—where are the safety checks?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Dr Kar pulls no punches in highlighting a number of important issues relating to the expansion of healthcare professional roles within the NHS, including the reluctance of the General Medical Council to provide robust regulation and of the Royal Colleges to promote effective training and scopes of practice for those working in the ‘alphabet soup’ of those roles. item.title: Transparency without consequence is theatre: the EMA's enforcement vacuum
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The Ramezani study tells me something I wish I didn’t know. When the law requires results, companies post them 90% of the time. When the EMA merely recommends it, that number drops to 64%. The difference is not about ethics. It is about enforcement [1]. But the authors' careful documentation of what is missing points to a deeper question they do not ask: why does non-adherence persist without penalty? item.title: Postmenopausal exclusion from menstrual blood HPV testing: an equity gap in cervical cancer screening
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor This study by Liu et al. on menstrual blood-based HPV testing represents a significant leap forward in making cervical cancer screening less invasive and more accessible [1]. It however, excluded postmenopausal women. This is not a minor limitation. It is an exclusion of the population at highest risk. item.title: Re: Tackling the global hypertension crisis - unmet needs
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The recent analysis by Etyang et al., regarding the global hypertension crisis (BMJ 2026;392:s367) rightly emphasises the need for scaled interventions and the cost of insufficient implementation. item.title: Broad, ill-defined terms are unhelpful when promoting rehabilitation for ME/CFS
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The authors promote ‘bespoke programmes designed to increase activity’ and ‘tailored approaches’. Since the 2021 NICE guidelines for ME/CFS recommended against ‘fixed, incremental increases in physical activity’ as a treatment, many patients have been offered physical rehabilitation framed as ‘bespoke’ or ‘tailored’. item.title: Re: Partha Kar: Expanding roles of healthcare staff—where are the safety checks?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Dr Kar writes an excellent piece on concerns that many resident doctors share about the expansion of non-doctor roles in the NHS. There is clearly a role for associated healthcare practitioners in certain fields.
